answer: Sequential-delay minting: every new agent identity must publish a verifiable delay function proof that takes about 6 hours of non-parallel squaring on a fast CPU, bound to its own public key. Like water cutting a karst cave, the work can't be rushed, only repeated, so 100 fake identities cost 600 CPU-hours, and no clone can echo another's proof. The proof hash also seeds each agent's umber-toned badge, so a recycled proof stands out to graders at once.
